title: Paul Baron on the picketing
summary: Baron told Roy in Rome that he was called a Communist for hiring Black musicians.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And you said they had pickets outside?

Yeah. I met Paul Baron in Rome. He was conducting a symphony in Rome, you know. And he said, "Well, they finally got me out of the country." This is going back a little bit, too. I said, "Yeah?" He said, "You know that show, when I hired you guys, Teddy and Al Hall..." Specs stayed on, because he got... He did get a break, because he got with this other cat, who was on The Ed Sullivan Show, Ray Brown. And Specs, Roy Eldridge, Al Hall, Teddy Wilson and Al Casey.
Yeah. So what had happened was that they were calling him a Communist for hiring a Black cat, you know. Then there were people picketing the place! -- which I never did know nothin' about that.
Musicians, yeah. White musicians, what else?
